newsitem.title: GERMANY: DAX trades sideways, volatility stymies ascent.
newsitem.headline: DAX trades sideways, volatility stymies ascent.

text.p: German shares moved mostly sideways at the beginning of bourse trade on Friday in a volatile market seeking direction but underpinned by the continued strength of the dollar and a higher Wall St close.
In early trade the DAX index was up 7.28 points, or 0.17 percent, at 4,343.02.
Dealers were hard pushed to come up with a forecast for the market, though trade was expected to be somewhat quieter.
"No one knows where this market is going at the moment. It's going up, it's going down, it's pretty unique at the moment and very volatile," a Frankfurt trader said.

The spectre of a possible interest rate rise haunted some market players, after the Bundesbank dropped a subtle hint to the markets that it could swing into action rapidly if a policy change were needed.

The central bank left its M3 money supply target and all of its main interest rates unchanged after its regular policy meeting on Thursday, but kept markets guessing as to where its main money market rate would be set in two weeks' time.
"If an interest rate rise comes, then the DAX is around 500 points too high," one trader said, although another trader said these fears were exaggerated.
Shares in the news included Siemens AG, which hit an all-time high in pre-bourse trade after a positive reaction to an analysts' meeting on Thursday.
Siemens was up 3.10 marks at 123.90 marks in bourse.
The banking sector was again centre of attention, with euphoria over the merger between Hypo-Bank and Vereinsbank still lifting the banks.
First-half results on Thursday also helped underpin sentiment in the sector.
Deutsche Bank AG was strongly ahead, up 3.78 pct at 123.50.
Commerzbank was up 2.20 marks at 65.20 marks, again boosted by merger speculation.
Retailer Metro AG was up 1.10 marks at 97 marks. Dealers said the stock had become more attractive since the recent share split, which had made the increased liquidity.

Shares in the sportswear maker Puma AG were down 35 pfennigs at 50.20 marks. The group earlier said it expected sales growth below 10 percent this year after turnover climbed six percent in the first half.
Dealers said that overall a quiet day was on the cards for the German share market after one of the most turbulent weeks in its history, with resistance pegged at around 4,400 points.
"For next week I expect the market to continue rising," a trader said.
